newsitem.title: JAPAN: PRESS DIGEST - Top Japan business news - Nov 22.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Top Japan business news - Nov 22.

text.p: Chief Cabinet Secretary Seiroku Kajiyama said a two trillion yen package of cuts in income tax and resident's tax will be ended by this fiscal year as planned, amid further signs of an economic recovery.
NEC Corp wins a contract worth about 30 billion yen to supply computer hardware and terminals for a 100 billion yen digital, multimedia cable service planned by Hong Kong Telecommunications Ltd.

The Bank of Japan will extend loans totalling several hundred billion yen to the Deposit Insurance Corp to help it write off losses left by the failure of Hanwa Bank Ltd and the Kizu and Osaka credit unions. Aggregate losses at the three institutions are expected to amount to more than 1.2 trillion yen, close to half the corporation's 2.5 trillion yen in expected income over five years.

Many companies in heavy industries, such as steelmaking and shipbuilding, are expected to be faced with the retirement of many of their employees in the near future. Ishikawajima-Harima Heavy Industries Co Ltd will see 40 percent of its workers, about 6,000 people, retire over the next 10 years when they reach 60. Over 40 percent of the technical staff at six steelmakers, including Nippon Steel Corp, will retire over the next decade.
